I read p.142 (with pp.30-32, 140-143) and the Lean source; no Lean was run. Auditor and both skeptics agree, and I concur. Every clause is stated: the cone on [terminalStart, tailEnd); the smooth direction and gap margin; (A.48)-(A.50) by exact factorizations with globally smooth coefficients; (A.51) by jet and lower bounds. The differences are packaging, explicit smallness thresholds that the paper's own proof uses, and (η,δ) coordinates. I added NominalConeAssembly.Witness.terminal_true and LeadingStressWeights.nominal_terminal_stress, which state the cone and the stress identity for the joined regular-axis profile, and replaced terminal_strict_direction by the stronger terminal_true_direction. The PAIRING skeptic regards the two nominal-profile theorems as consumers, not statements.

findings.summary: No single declaration states A.10. The cone, the direction collar, (A.48)-(A.50) and (A.51) are separate theorems, mostly about the backward-formula profileStress in (η,δ) coordinates. Bridge lemmas identify it with the actual leading stress.

Clause (i) and the full-interval gap margin carry explicit hypotheses: SmallTail (h ≤ 1/4, h ≤ 1/(1+releaseBudget)) and radiusThreshold F ≤ XR (switch radius ≥ 32). The paper's statement leaves these implicit; its proof invokes them.

terminal_forward_cone has no regular-axis hypothesis. It is about the concrete pre-axis outgoing family (Specification with ideal_prefix, CompensationWitness). The regular-axis statement exists for the joined nominal profile: Witness.terminal_true and nominal_terminal_stress.
The (A.51) bounds use iteratedFDeriv in edge coordinates (η,δ) and the sup norm on ℝ×ℝ. The paper's ∂^I are mixed derivatives in profile variables and |·| is Euclidean.
